request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every successful add or edit of a person or claim now writes one line to the audit file. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it works:** each of the four write endpoints gets one new final step, run just before the response:
- `RecordPersonAdded` and `RecordPersonEdited` in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/person/`
- `RecordClaimAdded` and `RecordClaimEdited` in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/claim/`

They're added to the four endpoint YAML files: `people.POST`, `people/{personId}.PUT`, `people/{personId}/claims.POST` and `claims/{claimId}.PUT`.

**Refusals write nothing:** a refused request throws an error at an earlier step, so it never reaches the audit step. Any rule added later should also go before that step, and it will then write nothing either.

**Line format:** the event, then `sheet=` and `by=` (the signed-in user), then the fields in the order you gave. Amounts are already stored with two decimals and dates as yyyy-mm-dd, so the lines match the screen. A claim line looks up the person's current name for `person=`.

**One limitation:** the audit line is written inside the database transaction, just before it commits. In the unlikely case that the commit itself fails, the audit file would have a line for a change that wasn't saved.

No database or front-end changes were needed. The front end already sends the signed-in user as `by` on every add and edit.
